description: An earlier ``espalier/managed_markers.py::has_managed_marker`` was a substring scan: it scanned the first ~600 chars for the bare token ``espalier:managed`` (``MANAGED_MARKER in content[:scan]``). A hostile asset shipped via PR or upstream dependency could plant the substring inside a YAML scalar (``description: "compatible with espalier:managed projects"``), a JSON string value, or a prose paragraph. On the next ``espalier init`` rerun, ``_deploy_asset_md`` would observe ``has_managed_marker(content) == True`` for the hostile file and overwrite it with the packaged copy — except that's wrong: the hostile file is the one masquerading as managed, so the operator's hand-authored content gets stomped, OR the operator's hand-authored hook that happens to mention the substring in a docstring gets regenerated and their edits silently disappear. Fix: anchor the regex to a comment-line start — ``^[ \t]*(?:#|<!--|::)[ \t]*espalier:managed\b`` with ``re.ASCII`` flag — so only canonical comment-line markers count as ownership signals. Substring forgeries in YAML scalars, prose, and JSON values no longer trigger recognition.
documented_in: tests/test_managed_markers.py::TestLineAnchoredRecognition (13 tests covering YAML-scalar / prose / JSON-value / alternate-comment-char / case-variant / mid-line / trailing-text / word-boundary / leading-tab / ZWSP-prefix forgeries plus canonical-form positives); tests/test_managed_markers.py::TestLegacySubstringHelperIsolated (2 tests asserting the deprecated _legacy_substring_match helper remains for migration assertion only)
